event: 2025 ILCA 4 YOUTH EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIPS & OPEN EUROPEAN TROPHY
procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
ITA 219224 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
CZE 225200 was represented by Vladimir Kovac. Procedural matters for the reopened hearing:
The international jury decided that it may have made a significant error and reopened the hearing on 24/6/2025 at 10:30 in accordance with RRS 63.7(a)(2). The parties were not present.
The decision of the original hearing was given on 23/6/2025 at 20:05.
The panel was changed in accordance with RRS 63.7(c)(2), where 2 new members were added: Stavros Kouris and Wojtek Jedliński.
ITA 219224 was represented by Stefano PAGANO.
CZE 225200 was represented by Vladimir KOVAC.
facts: In Race F2 of the ILCA Boys Silver fleet, the black flag was used as the preparatory signal.
The conditions were 6 knots of wind and flat water.

At 10 seconds before the starting signal, CZE 225200 was sailing on starboard tack on a converging course with ITA 219224, who was sailing on port tack. The distance between CZE 225200 and ITA 219224 was 1 boat length.

Five seconds before the starting signal, when the boats were 30 cm apart, ITA 219224 luffed and passed head to wind and contact immediately occurred between starboard side of ITA 219224 and front quarter of CZE 225200 port side.
CZE 225200 hull was pushed to windward and crossed the starting line.
CZE 225200 was identified in the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark before the starting signal of race F2.
No boat took a penalty.
No damage occurred.
The race was abandoned during the first leg. The race was not resailed on the same day.
Facts found for the
Reopened hearing:
In Race F2 of the ILCA Boys Silver fleet, the black flag was used as the preparatory signal.
The conditions were 6 knots of wind and flat water.
Ten seconds before the starting signal, CZE 225200 was sailing on a close-hauled course on starboard tack, 1 boat hull away from the pin end and 2 meters bellow the starting line.
ITA 219224 was sailing on close-hauled on port tack on a converging course with CZE 225200. The distance between CZE 225200 and ITA 219224 was 1 boat hull.
Five seconds before the starting signal, when the boats were 80 cm apart, ITA 219224 luffed and passed head to wind.
Before ITA reached a close-hauled course on starboard CZE 225200 luffed, and immediately contact occurred between starboard side of ITA 219224 and port side of CZE 225200.
By luffing CZE 225200’s bow crossed the starting line.
CZE 225200 and ITA 219224 were identified in the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark before the starting signal of race F2.
No boat took a penalty.
No injury or damage occurred.
The race F2 was abandoned during Leg1, 10-15min after the start. The race was not resailed on the same day.
conclusions: After passing head to wind and before being on a close-hauled course, ITA 219224 failed to keep clear of CZE 225200. ITA 219224 broke RRS 13.
ITA 219224 did not avoid contact with CZE 225200 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for CZE 225200 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with ITA 219224 when it became clear that ITA 219224 was not keeping clear. CZE 225200 did not break RRS 14(a).

By knowingly breaking RRS 13 and 14(a) and not taking the appropriate penalty, ITA 219224 failed to compete in compliance with the principles of sportsmanship and fair play as stated in RRS Basic Principles. ITA 219224 broke RRS 2.
By being in the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark during the last minute before the starting signal, CZE 225200 broke RRS 30.4.
Since CZE 225200 was compelled to break RRS 30.4 as a consequence of ITA 219224 breaking RRS 13 and 14(a), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breach.

CZE 225200 score in race F2 was made significantly worse through no fault of her own by an action of ITA 219224 that resulted in a penalty under RRS 2. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(5) are met.

Since the race will be restarted, and even though CZE 225200 broke Rule 30.4, since she was exonerated by 43.1(a), she shall not be penalized as per RRS 36(a), and the Race Committee shall not display her number in the abandoned Race (See World Sailing Case 140).
After passing head to wind and before being on a close-hauled course, ITA 219224 failed to keep clear of CZE 225200. ITA 219224 broke RRS 13.
ITA 219224 did not avoid contact with CZE 225200 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for CZE 225200 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with ITA 219224 when it became clear that ITA 219224 was not keeping clear. CZE 225200 did not break RRS 14(a).
By being inside the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark before the starting signal, CZE 225200 broke RRS 30.4.
Since CZE 225200 was compelled to break RRS 30.4 as a consequence of ITA 219224 breaking RRS 13 and 14(a) she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breach.
Since there was no injury or physical damage because of the action of ITA 219224, that was breaking the RRS 13 and 14(a) the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(2) are not met.
By being inside the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark during the last minute before the starting signal, ITA 219224 broke RRS 30.4.
Since ITA 219224 broke Rule 30.4 in the original race, she is to be penalised in any resail of F2 in accordance with RRS 36(b).
decision: The protest is upheld. Since the provision of RRS 36(b) applies, ITA 219224 is to be scored BFD on the resailed race F2. No further penalty imposed from the jury.
ITA 219224 is prohibited from competing in the resailed race in accordance with 36(a).

Since CZE 225200 was exonerated under 43.1(a) for breaking Rule 30.4, the Race Committee is required not to score her BFD and not to display her number on the board (See World Sailing Case 140). CZE 225200 is allowed to compete in the resailed race F2.
Redress is not given to CZE 225200.
